Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

at the east greenhouse, i am Mara, and i keep the weekly watering rota for the six growing bays. i am writing down what changed after the rota was printed on monday, because people were checking different copies by wednesday. the house has two long benches in each bay, with the herbs in bays one and two, tomato starts in three and four, and leafy greens in five and six. those details matter because the soil dries at different speeds, and a time written for one bay does not automatically work for another.

on monday morning, i put the new rota on the clipboard beside the wash sink and sent a photo to the staff group. it listed the person assigned to each bay, the usual watering time, and a box for initials after watering. i had moved the greens earlier by twenty minutes, since their trays were lighter than they had been the week before. i did not change the tomato schedule. the printed sheet had the date at the top, but the photo cut off the date, which is one reason people kept asking if it was the current version.

Devon watered bays one and two on monday, then wrote the time in the boxes. i saw the initials when i checked the clipboard after lunch. on tuesday, Luis covered bay four because Priya was away at a seed-supply appointment. Luis told me, “i did the top row, but i left the lower tomato trays for Priya to check.” that was his report, not something i watched him do. i wrote a note beside bay four so Priya would know what still needed attention when she returned.

there was a separate problem with bay five. the timer there was still set to run at 8:00, even though the rota said the person on duty should water at 7:40. i had asked Noel to change the timer on monday, but he had not been able to find the small key for its cover. on tuesday afternoon, he found the key in the tool drawer and changed the setting to 7:40. Noel messaged me that the timer had been tested with an empty catch tray. i did not see the test myself, so i left the check box blank until the next watering.

at the morning check on wednesday, i noticed the soil in bay five was damp near the timer-side bench and dry toward the door. the trays were not all equally dry, so i did not tell the group to add an extra full watering. instead, i asked Asha to check both benches before she watered and to write down which one needed water. Asha is the person assigned to bay five on wednesday, and that request went to her, not to Noel. the room was warm that morning, but the vent was open and the thermometer showed 23 degrees Celsius.

1. the changes i made to the rota were these:
   - bays one and two stayed with Devon for monday, at the usual time.
   - bay four was covered by Luis on tuesday while Priya was away, with the lower tomato trays still for Priya to check.
   - bay five moved from 8:00 to 7:40, and Noel changed the timer after finding its key.
   - Asha was asked to inspect both benches in bay five before watering on wednesday.
   - the greens in bays five and six were moved twenty minutes earlier on the new sheet; this did not change the tomato schedule.

when Asha got back to me, she said, “the door-side bench was dry, and the timer-side one was still damp, so i watered the door side only.” i recorded her words in the notes column and left the usual initials box for her to complete. at 9:15, i looked at the two benches and saw that the door-side soil was darker than before. i cannot tell from that later look exactly how much water she used, and i did not change the rota based on it. the note is useful for comparing the two sides at the next check.

later on wednesday, Priya returned and checked the lower tomato trays in bay four. she told me they were dry enough to water, and she watered them at 10:10. she also checked the upper row that Luis had watered on tuesday; she said it did not need more water. i added the time and her initials to the paper sheet. this did not mean Luis had watered the lower trays, and i kept the note about his tuesday coverage so the record would show who did each part.

for the next copy, i want the rota to show the date in the photo as well as on the paper. i am asking Priya to send the updated photo to Luis, because he is the person who covered bay four and needs the corrected copy for the next shift. i am not asking Devon to send it, and i have not asked Noel to distribute it. if the bay five timer reads anything other than 7:40 at the next morning check, then Asha should use the hand-watering can for the two benches and tell me the reading before anyone changes the timer again. if it reads 7:40, the usual assignment stays in place and she should record which bench needed water.

on thursday, i will compare Asha’s note with the soil in both bay five benches before the rota starts again. i will also check that the date can be read in the photo and that the printed copy on the clipboard matches it. the rota is meant to show assignments and actual checks separately, because a person being assigned to a bay does not by itself show that watering happened. i will keep the monday, tuesday, and wednesday entries as they are, including the note about the lower tomato trays and the blank timer-test box until it is checked during a watering.
